frontier.hypothesis: The ret seat is reachable by attacking it as a LOCAL-ALLOC problem: get the branch-condition and product temporaries out of $v0 in the windows where ret is live
frontier.mechanism: The seat reduces to exactly one graph edge - reg 96 conflicts with hard reg 2 - and that edge exists only because local_alloc gave $v0 to twelve short-lived quantities here while giving $v1 only four; record_one_conflict (global.c:1392) then IORs $v0 into reg 96's conflicts at one of ret's four births. The target does the reverse and returns in $v0 with no restore, so a C shape that flips local_alloc's choice closes both residual insns at once.
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/local-alloc.c find_free_reg and block_alloc to learn what makes a quantity take $v1 ahead of $v0 - qty_phys_copy_sugg and qty_phys_sugg are consulted before the ascending scan, so a quantity copied to or from a specific hard register gets that register first - then ask which C shape gives block 1's and block 2's condition quantity a $v1 suggestion. Make every future variant report its local_alloc map for free by dumping the ';; Register N in H.' lines from its .lreg alongside the sandbox score.

frontier.hypothesis: A permuter campaign seeded on r2 or q2 - distinct objects that tie at 26 - finds what the saturated base basin could not
frontier.mechanism: s5's perm_e saturated the base 26 basin (11,782 iterations, 9 novel finds, all semantically broken) but was seeded on the base object. There are now four distinct objects at the floor and only the base has been searched; q1, q2 and r2 are different source geometries compiling to different objects, so their neighbourhoods are different. Both floor drops on record (40 to 34 and 34 to 26) came from hand-repairing a semantically broken find, so a broken find here is a LEAD, not a failure.
frontier.next_probe: tmp/grind/func_8002E6B0/s5/mkws.sh (it carries the current -mel -msoft-float flags; the older tools/mar_perm_workspace.sh and the func_800283D0 copy predate soft-float) on memory/grind/func_8002E6B0/rejected/s7_cond_carrier_cross_point_distinct_object_ties_26.c and .../s6_first_if_xor_swap_distinct_object_ties_26.c, one fresh-seed window each, waited in-turn with tools/permuter_campaign.py wait and stopped with harvest --stop before the outcome is written. Do NOT re-seed the base 26 basin (perm_e) or the 34 basin (s4 perm_c). Read every find's SEMANTICS before scoring it.

frontier.hypothesis: The ra_solver suite becomes usable on this function once extract.py can supply a DIRECTIONAL conflict matrix (operator work, outside a grind session's allowed surface)
frontier.mechanism: prune_preferences uses the one-way conflict bit (global.c:920) while dump_conflicts prints the symmetric closure (global.c:1807); the model is built from the dump, so its regs_someone_prefers is strictly too large and the ord-0 seat is wrong on this function. Until that is fixed, every inverse.py verdict here is void - including the negative result s6 logged.
frontier.next_probe: Either add a birth-order proxy to tools/ra_solver/extract.py (row I of the matrix holds the allocnos already live when I was born, so first-def insn order approximates the direction) or add a cc1 hook that dumps the raw conflicts array alongside the existing ALLOCDBG/FINDREGDBG streams, then re-run simulate.py on tmp/ra_solver_work/func_8002E6B0.model.json and check it reproduces ord 0-2 (96 to $v1, 95 to $v0, 94 to $a0) before trusting any inverse verdict. In the meantime use BB2_FINDREG_DEBUG (tmp/grind/func_8002E6B0/s7/findreg.sh) as the ground-truth substitute.
